clue.text: Protestor seeking 6's encouraging shout for Beyoncé?

definitions.note: 6 down is a cut in tax, which is what the protesting rider demanded

parts.note: a cry urging someone on, as from a crowd
the singer is the very model of a pop diva

explanation.surface: A fan in the crowd yells encouragement at Beyoncé on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Godiva, by legend, rode naked through Coventry to make her husband lift a harsh tax, so she is a protestor after the 6-down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend makes Lady Godiva a famous campaigner against her husband's punitive levy on the townspeople.

clue.text: Cut diamonds in two different ways

parts.note: D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
diamonds are also ice in slang, so the same word is read a second time

explanation.surface: A jeweller cuts diamonds using two different techniques.
explanation.walkthrough: The word diamonds does double duty: once as the suit letter D, once as the slang ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dice food is to chop it into small cubes, a kind of cutting.

clue.text: Like Stalin's reign — go for reform with Nikita finally

indicators.note: reform means reshape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of Nikita

parts.note: taken as written; Khrushchev followed Stalin

explanation.surface: A historian notes that Stalin's rule needed reforming, as Nikita Khrushchev eventually did.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalin was born in Gori in Georgia, so he was a native of that country.

clue.text: Top spy infiltrates great corporation making outlandish products

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside, so the spy's letter goes within the other word

parts.note: ace means excellent or great
M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A spymaster gets inside a big firm known for its bizarre inventions.
explanation.walkthrough: Acme is the company in the Road Runner cartoons whose absurd gadgets Wile E. Coyote buys.
explanation.definitionFit: In Looney Tunes the Acme Corporation supplies rocket skates, giant magnets and other ridiculous contraptions.

clue.text: Weed the setter's knocked over, cut badly and rebuked

indicators.note: in a down clue, knocked over means flipped upside down so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the setter says I'm

indicators.note: badly means the letters of cut are mangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
to rate someone is an old word for scolding them

explanation.surface: Someone's weed has been knocked down, hacked at clumsily, and they have been told off for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Weed is not the plant but wee'd, the past tense of wee.
explanation.definitionFit: To wee is to urinate, and the answer is the formal medical verb for passing urine.

clue.text: A gift from Jeremy Hunt? Ta!

definitions.text: A gift from Jeremy Hunt? Ta!

parts.note: Jeremy Hunt was the UK Chancellor of the Exchequer, who sets taxes
a three-letter levy with its last letter chopped off leaves ta, the British slang thanks

explanation.surface: A grateful taxpayer thanks the Chancellor for his present.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta is British slang for thank you, but it is also what is left of TAX when it is cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduction in a levy is the kind of handout a Chancellor gives in a budget.

clue.text: E.g. sweet clothing old-fashioned solver's trying here

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping around, so the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: a sweet or dessert is one course of a meal
thou is the archaic word for you, the solver

explanation.surface: A solver dressed in old-fashioned clothes is attempting some sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is is, a link; trying here means the place where cases are tried.
explanation.definitionFit: A building that holds law courts is where defendants are put on trial.

clue.text: Light reader following case of eyestrain

indicators.note: following means the reader comes after the other piece
the case of a word is its outside, so take the first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written
a Kindle is Amazon's e-reader

explanation.surface: Someone reads a Kindle after a bout of eyestrain and needs a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: To enkindle a fire is to set it alight, so the verb is a synonym of ignite.

clue.text: This possibly leads to extra virgin oil?

definitions.text: This possibly leads to extra virgin oil?

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters could be arranged another way
the leads of words are their first letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wry question about where extra virgin oil comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes the fruit pressed for extra virgin oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra virgin oil is pressed from this fruit, so it is literally what leads to the oil.

clue.text: London's easternmost area?

parts.note: London has a district by this name in Soho, in the West End
read as the most Eastern, Oriental, part of town, not the most easterly

explanation.surface: A geography question about which district lies furthest east in London.
explanation.walkthrough: The district is in the West End, so easternmost refers to its East Asian character, not its position.
explanation.definitionFit: London's Chinese quarter, around Gerrard Street, is the most Oriental area of the capital.

clue.text: Not messing about, I approach and then retreat

parts.note: taken as written
to near something is to approach it
a nest is a cosy refuge or retreat

explanation.surface: Someone serious describes advancing and then backing off.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in earnest means being sincere and serious, rather than joking around.

clue.text: Parts of a joint of beef and last of pastrami

parts.note: to beef is to complain, as is to carp

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A butcher lists cuts of beef and the end of a pastrami.
explanation.walkthrough: Joint looks like a roast, and beef like meat; here beef is a verb for complaining.
explanation.definitionFit: The carpals are the small bones of the wrist, which is a joint of the arm.

clue.text: Funny couple of Americans visiting Germany

parts.note: two abbreviations for American, AM and US
someone visiting a place is in it
G is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Two American tourists have an amusing time in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amusing is entertaining and makes people laugh, so it is comic.

clue.text: Gauche article in El País by European journalist

parts.note: un is the Spanish indefinite article, and El País is a Spanish newspaper
a Pole is Polish
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A Spanish newspaper prints a clumsy piece by a European reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: El País is Spain's leading daily, so article means a word like un, not a news story.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpolished means lacking refinement, which is what gauche, awkward and socially clumsy, describes.

clue.text: They hunt old badgers

parts.note: grey hair suggests old age
to hound someone is to pester, or badger, them

explanation.surface: Elderly badgers are on the prowl for food.
explanation.walkthrough: Badgers is not the animal but a verb for nagging.
explanation.definitionFit: Greyhounds are sight hounds bred for coursing hares, so they are dogs used in the chase.

clue.text: Did gag in opening of routine and made an impression

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
to etch is to cut a design into a surface

explanation.surface: A comedian told a joke at the start of the act and it went down well.
explanation.walkthrough: Gag looks like a joke, but here it is the verb for heaving.
explanation.definitionFit: To retch is to strain to vomit, which is what gagging means.

clue.text: Plead with sentenced criminal to take heart in tough part of sentence

indicators.note: criminal suggests these letters have been bent out of shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A defence lawyer urges a convicted offender to stay strong in a hard part of his jail term.
explanation.walkthrough: Sentence switches from a prison term in the surface to a grammatical sentence in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dependent clause is a grammatical unit that cannot stand alone and forms part of a larger sentence.

clue.text: Torrid dancing with publicity for country track

indicators.note: dancing letters jump around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
an ad publicises something

explanation.surface: A steamy dance routine gets press coverage for a country music song.
explanation.walkthrough: Country track suggests a song; it is a rural road.
explanation.definitionFit: An unpaved road in the countryside is a rough rural track.

clue.text: Primo Levi's beginning extremely amazing novel in which a character's missing

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Praise for the opening of a brilliant book by the Italian writer Primo Levi, in which a person has disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: Character means a letter of the alphabet, not a person in the story.
explanation.definitionFit: A lipogram is a text written deliberately without one letter, such as Perec's novel avoiding the letter E.

clue.text: Head girl wanting day off in US capital

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the remaining letters are jumbled
wanting means lacking, so the letter for day is taken out

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A school head girl wants a day off to visit an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Raleigh is the state capital of North Carolina, so it is a capital city in the United States.

clue.text: Italy's capital I see, and possibly Berlin

parts.note: I is the international code for Italy, and the 's gives S
capital as an exclamation means excellent, A1, with the 1 written as I
ah is the sound of sudden understanding

explanation.surface: A traveller reaches Rome, says they understand, and perhaps moves on to Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: Berlin is not the city but the philosopher Isaiah Berlin; capital! is an old exclamation for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Isaiah Berlin was the Oxford philosopher, so Berlin is an example of a bearer of this first name.

clue.text: On the move, I depart and fly in this group

indicators.note: letters on the move shift around into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller announces they are leaving and flying off with a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Diptera is the insect order of the true flies, the two-winged insects.

clue.text: A place like Park Avenue or Wall Street still

parts.note: taken as written

parts.words: place like Park Avenue or Wall Street
parts.note: both are streets, or ways, in New York, NY

explanation.surface: A description of a smart Manhattan address.
explanation.walkthrough: Park Avenue looks like a London Monopoly square; here both are New York thoroughfares.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyway and still are both adverbs meaning nevertheless or in any case.

clue.text: Dreaded figure, someone like Boris making comeback

indicators.note: coming back means running in reverse, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: Boris Godunov was a tsar of Russia

explanation.surface: A feared politician called Boris is staging a return.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris suggests Johnson, but it is Boris Godunov; dreaded means wearing dreadlocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rastafarian is often pictured wearing dreadlocks, so is literally a dreadlocked person.

clue.text: Looking rough, you reportedly head for Soho during every evening

indicators.note: reportedly tells you to go by how the word is spoken

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: during puts the letter in the middle of the other piece

parts.note: nightly means each night

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written; Soho is a London nightlife district

explanation.surface: You look a mess, apparently, from going out to Soho every night.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsightly means unpleasant to look at, which is what a rough appearance is.

clue.text: Maybe Murdoch's revolutionary virtual assistant

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Iris Murdoch was the novelist, so Murdoch is a surname she bore

explanation.surface: Rupert Murdoch's radical new digital helper.
explanation.walkthrough: Murdoch suggests the media tycoon Rupert, but it is the novelist Iris.
explanation.definitionFit: Siri is Apple's voice-controlled software helper on iPhones.

clue.text: Perhaps these emitted liquid when turned?

definitions.text: Perhaps these emitted liquid when turned?

indicators.note: turned means reversed, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: spat means ejected saliva

explanation.surface: A question about whether faucets flowed once opened.
explanation.definitionFit: Taps release water when their handles are rotated, so they are fittings that spout once opened.

clue.text: Pope has a lover, admitting evidence of wrongdoing?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the cross goes inside the lover

parts.note: Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to his lover Hero
a cross marks a wrong answer

explanation.surface: A scandal: the Pontiff has a mistress and confesses to sin.
explanation.walkthrough: Pope is not the pontiff but the poet Alexander Pope, though there were Pope Alexanders too.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander was the first name of the poet Pope, and of several popes.

clue.text: The first Letter to the Corinthians?

definitions.text: The first Letter to the Corinthians?

parts.note: reads like the title of Paul's epistle, First Corinthians
Corinth was a Greek city, so its people wrote in Greek characters

explanation.surface: A reference to Saint Paul's first epistle in the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: First Corinthians is a book of the New Testament; here letter means a character of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the opening character of the Greek alphabet, which the Corinthians used.
